issue.title: Dangerous site: subscription traps via deceptive search advertising (chat-box.ai, chatboxinfo.com, use.ai)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

Other ad blocker

### AdGuard version

n/a, not an AdGuard product, see comment

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Dangerous site

### Which browser(s) do you use?

Chrome

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://chat-box.ai/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

_No response_

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

### Please read this first, it affects how the fields above should be read

I do not use an AdGuard product. I run the **AdGuard/Firebog blocklist inside OPNsense Unbound
DNSBL**, rebuilt daily, alongside other DNS blocklists. Three mandatory fields do not apply to
that setup, so rather than let them stand as claims:

- **AdGuard version:** entered as not applicable. There is no AdGuard product here to version.
- **Ad Blocking filter:** I had to pick one of three browser filters. I run none of them. I
  chose AdGuard Base filter only because it is the list that feeds the AdGuard DNS filter,
  which is the nearest thing to what I actually use.
- **"AdGuard product version is up-to-date":** ticked only because the form will not submit
  otherwise. My filter data is current, rebuilt daily. There is no product.

If a dangerous-site report from outside the AdGuard product ecosystem is out of scope, that is
a fair call and I would rather be told than have this quietly weighted as unreliable.

### The domains

```
chat-box.ai
chatboxinfo.com
use.ai
```

Only one fitted the URL field above.

### What they are

Two unrelated operators running the same playbook: **subscription traps acquired through paid
search advertising that trades on another company's product names**. Both are real, registered,
operating businesses that resell genuine AI model access, so this is not a report of malicious
or compromised infrastructure. In both cases a real person was billed.

The mechanism, and the reason DNS blocking is the only control that reaches it: **no email is
ever sent.** Not at signup, not when the trial converts, not for the charge. The only record of
the subscription anywhere is a line on a card statement. Cancellation is the first time either
operator writes to the customer.

**chat-box.ai / chatboxinfo.com.** A trial taken 2026-07-29 converted 2026-08-09 to USD 29.99
without notice. The advertiser's own tracking parameters, preserved in the landing URL, name
their target: `utm_term=claude` and a campaign named for the vendor and its product. Eleven days
passed between card capture and the charge with no email of any kind. After cancellation the
merchant sent two emails within 34 seconds, so its transactional mail works.

`chatboxinfo.com` is the billing descriptor, and it redirects to the operator's cancellation
page. Verifiable in one command:

```
$ curl -sI https://chatboxinfo.com/ | grep -i ^location
location: https://chat-box.ai/cancel
```

It exists to catch cardholders who type an unfamiliar statement line into a browser.

The operator's own name cannot be found on its own site. The company name and address on
`chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/` are published as images, not text, so they cannot be
searched, copied or indexed:

```
$ curl -s https://chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/ | grep -ic apollo
0
```

The name is Apollo Technology Global LLC, Wyoming filing 2024-001458375.

**use.ai.** Same pattern, different operator. Billed A$41.99/month after an advertised A$1.00
trial that actually billed A$0.95 twice. The search ad's display URL shows a breadcrumb path
that does not exist on the site. The recurring price appears only in small grey text, roughly
double two other plans shown more prominently. Its own cancellation page returned "temporarily
unavailable" while billing continued. Delaware corporation 10233757, incorporated 20 June 2025;
the domain dates from 2017 but changed hands 2025-09-29, so an operation about a year old wears
an eight year old domain, which defeats newly-registered-domain heuristics by design.

### Why blocking the domain is the only control

The click originates from `bing.com/aclick`, the same host as the search results, so the ad
cannot be filtered at DNS level. The destination domain is the only thing that can be blocked,
and because no email is ever sent, a household's first warning is a card statement weeks later.

Both sites do state somewhere that they are not affiliated with the model vendors, but that
text is reachable only after the click. The purchase decision is made from the ad.

### Status in your lists

Checked 2026-08-26 against `AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt` (179,421 lines, HTTP 200
confirmed before matching): all three absent.

### Full evidence

Submitted to Hagezi as issue #11253 with the complete write-up, including the advertiser
campaign identifiers, the registry records and the list-coverage table:
<https://github.com/hagezi/dns-blocklists/issues/11253>

Screenshots are available on request. I have not attached them unasked.


### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

issue.title: Dangerous site: subscription traps via deceptive search advertising (chat-box.ai, chatboxinfo.com, use.ai)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

Other ad blocker

### AdGuard version

n/a, not an AdGuard product, see comment

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Dangerous site

### Which browser(s) do you use?

Chrome

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://chat-box.ai/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

_No response_

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

### Please read this first, it affects how the fields above should be read

I do not use an AdGuard product. I run the **AdGuard/Firebog blocklist inside OPNsense Unbound
DNSBL**, rebuilt daily, alongside other DNS blocklists. Three mandatory fields do not apply to
that setup, so rather than let them stand as claims:

- **AdGuard version:** entered as not applicable. There is no AdGuard product here to version.
- **Ad Blocking filter:** I had to pick one of three browser filters. I run none of them. I
  chose AdGuard Base filter only because it is the list that feeds the AdGuard DNS filter,
  which is the nearest thing to what I actually use.
- **"AdGuard product version is up-to-date":** ticked only because the form will not submit
  otherwise. My filter data is current, rebuilt daily. There is no product.

If a dangerous-site report from outside the AdGuard product ecosystem is out of scope, that is
a fair call and I would rather be told than have this quietly weighted as unreliable.

### The domains

```
chat-box.ai
chatboxinfo.com
use.ai
```

Only one fitted the URL field above.

### What they are

Two unrelated operators running the same playbook: **subscription traps acquired through paid
search advertising that trades on another company's product names**. Both are real, registered,
operating businesses that resell genuine AI model access, so this is not a report of malicious
or compromised infrastructure. In both cases a real person was billed.

The mechanism, and the reason DNS blocking is the only control that reaches it: **no email is
ever sent.** Not at signup, not when the trial converts, not for the charge. The only record of
the subscription anywhere is a line on a card statement. Cancellation is the first time either
operator writes to the customer.

**chat-box.ai / chatboxinfo.com.** A trial taken 2026-07-29 converted 2026-08-09 to USD 29.99
without notice. The advertiser's own tracking parameters, preserved in the landing URL, name
their target: `utm_term=claude` and a campaign named for the vendor and its product. Eleven days
passed between card capture and the charge with no email of any kind. After cancellation the
merchant sent two emails within 34 seconds, so its transactional mail works.

`chatboxinfo.com` is the billing descriptor, and it redirects to the operator's cancellation
page. Verifiable in one command:

```
$ curl -sI https://chatboxinfo.com/ | grep -i ^location
location: https://chat-box.ai/cancel
```

It exists to catch cardholders who type an unfamiliar statement line into a browser.

The operator's own name cannot be found on its own site. The company name and address on
`chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/` are published as images, not text, so they cannot be
searched, copied or indexed:

```
$ curl -s https://chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/ | grep -ic apollo
0
```

The name is Apollo Technology Global LLC, Wyoming filing 2024-001458375.

**use.ai.** Same pattern, different operator. Billed A$41.99/month after an advertised A$1.00
trial that actually billed A$0.95 twice. The search ad's display URL shows a breadcrumb path
that does not exist on the site. The recurring price appears only in small grey text, roughly
double two other plans shown more prominently. Its own cancellation page returned "temporarily
unavailable" while billing continued. Delaware corporation 10233757, incorporated 20 June 2025;
the domain dates from 2017 but changed hands 2025-09-29, so an operation about a year old wears
an eight year old domain, which defeats newly-registered-domain heuristics by design.

### Why blocking the domain is the only control

The click originates from `bing.com/aclick`, the same host as the search results, so the ad
cannot be filtered at DNS level. The destination domain is the only thing that can be blocked,
and because no email is ever sent, a household's first warning is a card statement weeks later.

Both sites do state somewhere that they are not affiliated with the model vendors, but that
text is reachable only after the click. The purchase decision is made from the ad.

### Status in your lists

Checked 2026-08-26 against `AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt` (179,421 lines, HTTP 200
confirmed before matching): all three absent.

### Full evidence

Submitted to Hagezi as issue #11253 with the complete write-up, including the advertiser
campaign identifiers, the registry records and the list-coverage table:
<https://github.com/hagezi/dns-blocklists/issues/11253>

Screenshots are available on request. I have not attached them unasked.


### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

issue.title: Dangerous site: subscription traps via deceptive search advertising (chat-box.ai, chatboxinfo.com, use.ai)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

Other ad blocker

### AdGuard version

n/a, not an AdGuard product, see comment

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Dangerous site

### Which browser(s) do you use?

Chrome

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://chat-box.ai/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

_No response_

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

### Please read this first, it affects how the fields above should be read

I do not use an AdGuard product. I run the **AdGuard/Firebog blocklist inside OPNsense Unbound
DNSBL**, rebuilt daily, alongside other DNS blocklists. Three mandatory fields do not apply to
that setup, so rather than let them stand as claims:

- **AdGuard version:** entered as not applicable. There is no AdGuard product here to version.
- **Ad Blocking filter:** I had to pick one of three browser filters. I run none of them. I
  chose AdGuard Base filter only because it is the list that feeds the AdGuard DNS filter,
  which is the nearest thing to what I actually use.
- **"AdGuard product version is up-to-date":** ticked only because the form will not submit
  otherwise. My filter data is current, rebuilt daily. There is no product.

If a dangerous-site report from outside the AdGuard product ecosystem is out of scope, that is
a fair call and I would rather be told than have this quietly weighted as unreliable.

### The domains

```
chat-box.ai
chatboxinfo.com
use.ai
```

Only one fitted the URL field above.

### What they are

Two unrelated operators running the same playbook: **subscription traps acquired through paid
search advertising that trades on another company's product names**. Both are real, registered,
operating businesses that resell genuine AI model access, so this is not a report of malicious
or compromised infrastructure. In both cases a real person was billed.

The mechanism, and the reason DNS blocking is the only control that reaches it: **no email is
ever sent.** Not at signup, not when the trial converts, not for the charge. The only record of
the subscription anywhere is a line on a card statement. Cancellation is the first time either
operator writes to the customer.

**chat-box.ai / chatboxinfo.com.** A trial taken 2026-07-29 converted 2026-08-09 to USD 29.99
without notice. The advertiser's own tracking parameters, preserved in the landing URL, name
their target: `utm_term=claude` and a campaign named for the vendor and its product. Eleven days
passed between card capture and the charge with no email of any kind. After cancellation the
merchant sent two emails within 34 seconds, so its transactional mail works.

`chatboxinfo.com` is the billing descriptor, and it redirects to the operator's cancellation
page. Verifiable in one command:

```
$ curl -sI https://chatboxinfo.com/ | grep -i ^location
location: https://chat-box.ai/cancel
```

It exists to catch cardholders who type an unfamiliar statement line into a browser.

The operator's own name cannot be found on its own site. The company name and address on
`chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/` are published as images, not text, so they cannot be
searched, copied or indexed:

```
$ curl -s https://chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/ | grep -ic apollo
0
```

The name is Apollo Technology Global LLC, Wyoming filing 2024-001458375.

**use.ai.** Same pattern, different operator. Billed A$41.99/month after an advertised A$1.00
trial that actually billed A$0.95 twice. The search ad's display URL shows a breadcrumb path
that does not exist on the site. The recurring price appears only in small grey text, roughly
double two other plans shown more prominently. Its own cancellation page returned "temporarily
unavailable" while billing continued. Delaware corporation 10233757, incorporated 20 June 2025;
the domain dates from 2017 but changed hands 2025-09-29, so an operation about a year old wears
an eight year old domain, which defeats newly-registered-domain heuristics by design.

### Why blocking the domain is the only control

The click originates from `bing.com/aclick`, the same host as the search results, so the ad
cannot be filtered at DNS level. The destination domain is the only thing that can be blocked,
and because no email is ever sent, a household's first warning is a card statement weeks later.

Both sites do state somewhere that they are not affiliated with the model vendors, but that
text is reachable only after the click. The purchase decision is made from the ad.

I do not use an AdGuard product. I run the **AdGuard/Firebog blocklist inside OPNsense Unbound
DNSBL**, rebuilt daily, alongside other DNS blocklists. Three mandatory fields do not apply to
that setup, so rather than let them stand as claims:

- **AdGuard version:** entered as not applicable. There is no AdGuard product here to version.

  chose AdGuard Base filter only because it is the list that feeds the AdGuard DNS filter,
  which is the nearest thing to what I actually use.

  otherwise. My filter data is current, rebuilt daily. There is no product.

If a dangerous-site report from outside the AdGuard product ecosystem is out of scope, that is
a fair call and I would rather be told than have this quietly weighted as unreliable.

### The domains

```
chat-box.ai
chatboxinfo.com
use.ai
```

Only one fitted the URL field above.

### What they are

Two unrelated operators running the same playbook: **subscription traps acquired through paid
search advertising that trades on another company's product names**. Both are real, registered,
operating businesses that resell genuine AI model access, so this is not a report of malicious
or compromised infrastructure. In both cases a real person was billed.

The mechanism, and the reason DNS blocking is the only control that reaches it: **no email is
ever sent.** Not at signup, not when the trial converts, not for the charge. The only record of
the subscription anywhere is a line on a card statement. Cancellation is the first time either
operator writes to the customer.

**chat-box.ai / chatboxinfo.com.** A trial taken 2026-07-29 converted 2026-08-09 to USD 29.99
without notice. The advertiser's own tracking parameters, preserved in the landing URL, name
their target: `utm_term=claude` and a campaign named for the vendor and its product. Eleven days
passed between card capture and the charge with no email of any kind. After cancellation the
merchant sent two emails within 34 seconds, so its transactional mail works.

`chatboxinfo.com` is the billing descriptor, and it redirects to the operator's cancellation
page. Verifiable in one command:

```
$ curl -sI https://chatboxinfo.com/ | grep -i ^location
location: https://chat-box.ai/cancel
```

It exists to catch cardholders who type an unfamiliar statement line into a browser.

The operator's own name cannot be found on its own site. The company name and address on
`chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/` are published as images, not text, so they cannot be
searched, copied or indexed:

```
$ curl -s https://chat-box.ai/terms-and-conditions/ | grep -ic apollo
0
```

The name is Apollo Technology Global LLC, Wyoming filing 2024-001458375.

**use.ai.** Same pattern, different operator. Billed A$41.99/month after an advertised A$1.00
trial that actually billed A$0.95 twice. The search ad's display URL shows a breadcrumb path
that does not exist on the site. The recurring price appears only in small grey text, roughly
double two other plans shown more prominently. Its own cancellation page returned "temporarily
unavailable" while billing continued. Delaware corporation 10233757, incorporated 20 June 2025;
the domain dates from 2017 but changed hands 2025-09-29, so an operation about a year old wears
an eight year old domain, which defeats newly-registered-domain heuristics by design.

### Why blocking the domain is the only control

The click originates from `bing.com/aclick`, the same host as the search results, so the ad
cannot be filtered at DNS level. The destination domain is the only thing that can be blocked,
and because no email is ever sent, a household's first warning is a card statement weeks later.

Both sites do state somewhere that they are not affiliated with the model vendors, but that
text is reachable only after the click. The purchase decision is made from the ad.

### Status in your lists

Checked 2026-08-26 against `AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt` (179,421 lines, HTTP 200
confirmed before matching): all three absent.

### Full evidence

Submitted to Hagezi as issue #11253 with the complete write-up, including the advertiser
campaign identifiers, the registry records and the list-coverage table:
<https://github.com/hagezi/dns-blocklists/issues/11253>

Screenshots are available on request. I have not attached them unasked.

comment.body:
I've found the reason. The self-promo content is served under `nkis.nikkei.com`, which is blocked by adserver.txt in JapaneseFilter.

I have listed self-promotion requests below, but they didn't work due to `||nkis.nikkei.com`.

```adblock
! nikkei.com self-promo widget [data-kad-id="5226_7151"][data-kad-type="trendwatch"], confirmed serving content
@@||nkis.nikkei.com/ad?*section_id=7151&*$domain=nikkei.com
@@||nkis.nikkei.com/ad?*section_id=7153&*$domain=nikkei.com
@@||nkis.nikkei.com/ad?*section_id=10810&*$domain=nikkei.com
@@||nkis.nikkei.com/ad?*section_id=7155&*$domain=nikkei.com
!
! nikkei.com self-promo widget [data-kad-id="5225_7149"][data-kad-type="infeed-wide"]
@@||nkis.nikkei.com/ad?*section_id=7149&*$domain=nikkei.com
```

> Request URL example: `nkis.nikkei.com/ad?ord=6724574257231&section_id=7149&handler_name=process_tag_provider_response_7149`

What should I do about this issue?

Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

How to reproduce:

Go to a spam site and enter your email address to be put on a spam list

Check your SPAM folder for Gambling emails
Copy (NEVER visit) the domains and paste them below to help out other members:

freeflowducts.com
trackallnotifrewa.com
trustus-eu.uk
adv.bestyofr.store

Wait to get how to reproduce message back from some ID10T.
Go to hospital for one day.
Receive another Github email from the same ID10T who has close it.

### Proposed solution

Someone to add these domains to the list to block or NEVER report any other filters to the Adguard people.

### Additional information

New spam domains added daily.

IN THE DNS FILTER, THERE IS A SPELLING MISTAKE IN ONE OF THE COMMENTS.

Use AdGuard for Mac with HTTPS filtering enabled. > 2. Enable the **AdGuard Annoyances filter**. > 3. Disable DNS Protection. > 4. Disable the AdGuard Base filter. > 5. Ensure there is no user rule allowing `c2consulting.co.nz`. > 6. Open `https://c2consulting.co.nz/` in Firefox. > 7. The connection fails. > 8. Disable the AdGuard Annoyances filter and reload the same URL — the site loads normally. > > The AdGuard Filtering Log shows the following rule being applied to the site's HTML request: > > `/.*/$permissions=identity-credentials-get=(),document` > > Filter: **AdGuard Annoyances filter** > > I was able to confirm that adding this domain-specific exception restores the site while leaving the Annoyances filter enabled: > > `c2consulting.co.nz#@$permissions=identity-credentials-get` > > This appears to indicate that the `$permissions=identity-credentials-get=(),document` rule is incompatible with this site/Firefox configuration. > > The site is a legitimate website and does not require `identity-credentials-get` to be blocked for it to function. > > Please investigate whether this rule should apply to this domain, or whether the filter rule can be adjusted to avoid breaking the site's HTTPS connection in Firefox. ### Screenshots

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS.
